reference_text:
Welcome to the course. We will work through each concept carefully, connect the
ideas step by step, and use practical examples to make technical topics easier
to understand. When we introduce a new method, focus first on the problem it
solves and why it is useful. For example, in machine learning, features are the
information we give the model, while the target is what we want it to predict.
Now consider a simple question: what changes when the data contains missing
values? We will think through the reason and then look at the code. In Python,
we can inspect the data, run one small step at a time, and explain what the
result means. The goal is to understand the logic, not simply memorize syntax.

slides.title: Statistics & Visualization
slides.transcript:
Welcome to Module 13. Here we connect statistics with visualization and interpretation. We will summarize center and spread, examine distributions, compare groups, discuss correlation and uncertainty, and choose visual forms that fit the analytical question.

[tts-break]

Choose the visual based on the question: bars for categories, lines for time, histograms for distributions, and scatter plots for relationships.

slides.title: How to use this page
slides.transcript:
Use this lesson actively. Read the idea first and make a prediction before running any code. When a Python cell is available, click Run, inspect the output, and then change one small value or condition. Run it again and explain what changed. This predict, run, modify, and explain cycle is more useful than copying a finished example.

[tts-break]

Separate calculation from interpretation. A statistic summarizes the sample and a visualization reveals pattern, but both still require context, variability, and awareness of limitations.

[tts-break]

Before moving on, explain the main idea in one sentence without reading the slide. That quick explanation is a useful check that the concept is becoming reusable knowledge.

slides.title: Descriptive statistics
slides.transcript:
On this slide, we are focusing on descriptive statistics. Start with the meaning of the idea before worrying about the exact syntax. Ask what information is going in, what Python is doing with it, and what result should come out.

[tts-break]

Descriptive statistics summarize a dataset. Mean and median describe center, while range and standard deviation describe spread.

[tts-break]

Before clicking Run, predict the statistic or pattern you expect. After it runs, interpret the result in words. Then change one value and see whether the interpretation changes. Focus on meaning and limitations, not only the calculation.

[tts-break]
